title: Enable Push Notification Support in Receiving App for New Transfer Orders
body:
## What is the motivation for adding/enhancing this feature?

Currently, the Receiving App does not notify users when a new transfer order becomes available for receiving. Users must manually open the app and refresh to check for new transfer orders, which can lead to delays in the receiving process. Enabling push notifications will allow receiving users to be informed in real time whenever a new transfer order is available, improving operational efficiency and responsiveness.

---

## What are the acceptance criteria?

* [ ] Push notification support is enabled in the Receiving App.
* [ ] A push notification is sent when a new transfer order becomes available for receiving.
* [ ] Notifications are sent only to devices/users that have subscribed (opted in).
* [ ] Notification is received when the app is in foreground, background, or closed.
* [ ] Each transfer order triggers only one notification (no duplicates).
* [ ] Notification message clearly indicates that a new transfer order is available for receiving.

---

title: UI modal for the proof of delivery
body:
This ticket is for the UI change needed for the Proof of delivery in this application

Description
We need a Proof of Delivery (POD) feature in OMS to record and confirm that a customer (or their authorized representative) has picked up an order. This feature should capture proof of identity and generate a confirmation email to the customer.

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
1. Customer Confirmation at Pickup
Store associate asks the customer to confirm order details at pickup.
Customer provides proof of identity (e.g., ID upload, signature, or unique code).
The system records this confirmation and links it to the order.
2. Email Notification
Once confirmation is saved, an automated email is sent to the customer notifying them that the order has been picked up.
Email should include order details and confirmation of pickup.

Fix: Prevent SystemMessage Status Update to Null in process#BulkOperationResult
body:
Adding a null check for the `statusId` in `process#BulkOperationResult` before attempting to update the `SystemMessage` entity.

**Changes:**
- Added `statusId` variable to capture the mapped status.
- Added a condition `if (statusId)` to prevent service calls when the status mapping is null (e.g., for 'running' or 'created' statuses).

Fixes #252

linkedIssues.body:
In `process#BulkOperationResult`, the `statusMap` is defined as:
`[completed:'SmsgConfirmed', canceled:'SmsgCancelled', failed:'SmsgError', expired:'SmsgError']`

It does not contain keys for `running` or `created`. When `statusMap.get(status)` is called for these statuses (which are common during polling), it returns `null`. The service then proceeds to call `update#moqui.service.message.SystemMessage` with `statusId: null`.

**Problem**
Because of this, the `statusId` gets set to `null`. Once a message reaches this state, it never gets picked up or processed again. Essentially, the workflow breaks silently — no error is thrown, but the message is stuck forever.

**Proposed Solution:**
Add a condition to check if the mapped `statusId` is not null before invoking the update service.
linkedIssues.title: Prevent SystemMessage Status Update to Null in process#BulkOperationResult

title: Handled the condition to calc correct WAC when the oldTotalCost is a negative value
body: closes #238

linkedIssues.body:
Multiple instances have been identified where the Weighted Average Cost (WAC) is being incorrectly calculated as **0** in OMS after processing receiving transactions (Return / PO / TO).


### **Case 1: Negative QOH Resulting in Incorrect WAC**
**Issue:**  
The product initially had QOH = 0. A POS sale resulted in a negative QOH. After receiving a single unit, the system recalculated WAC and set it to **0**.

**Example:**  
[M102506](https://mephisto-oms.hotwax.io/commerce/control/ProductInventoryView?facilityId=488_MADISON&productId=M102506&facilityGroupId=FAC_GRP&groupByInventoryItem=false)


### **Case 2: Product Had NULL WAC**
There was no existing record for the product and facility in `ProductAverageCost`.  
When a return was received, the system calculated WAC using only the return transaction and assigned a value of **0**.

> This case is already handled in this [PR](https://github.com/hotwax/hotwax-oms/pull/197), [PR](https://github.com/hotwax/hotwax-oms/issues/184).

**Example:**  
[20651](https://mephisto-oms.hotwax.io/commerce/control/ProductInventoryView?productId=20651&groupByInventoryItem=false&facilityId=305_SEABOARD_LANE&facilityGroupId=FAC_GRP)


### **Case 3: Valid WAC Exists but Recalculated as Zero**
The product had a valid WAC in PAC. After receiving stock, OMS recalculated the WAC and set it to **0** because the computed result was negative, and the service defaults negative values to zero.

## **Observation**
In this WAC formula:
```
              ( ( Old_WAC * Old_QOH ) + ( Unit_Cost * Received_Qty ) )
WAC   =          ____________________________________________________
                             ( Old_QOH + Received_Qty )
```


- When **( Old_WAC × Old_QOH ) < 1**, the service calculates WAC as **0**.
- When **( Old_QOH + Received_Qty ) < 1**, the service also calculates WAC as **0**.

## Possible Solution:

- If WAC does not exist, use the Unit Cost from the receiving as the WAC.
- If (Old_WAC * Old_QOH) < 1, keep the existing WAC as the updated WAC.

body:

   1. Receive Quantity

      2. Complete quantity - status update

      1. With quantity
      2. Without quantity
   3. Receive New Product

title: Improved: Reconcile Transfer Order Receipts
body: Closes #128

linkedIssues.body:
### Problem Description

The existing `reconcile#ShipmentReceipts` service was written to handle only the simple scenario where a Transfer Order (TO) item is received before the shipment is created, and both have the same quantity.

However, we now have more complex cases:

- Over-receiving: the received quantity is greater than the shipped/ordered quantity.
- Multi-shipment fulfillment: a TO item is split across multiple shipments, but the user receives everything together in a single combined receipt.

In these scenarios, the current logic does not properly split received quantities or assign them correctly to shipments.

### Solution

The reconciliation logic must:

- Split the received quantity across shipments based on available shipment quantities.
- Update the existing receipt with the quantity matched to the first shipment.
- Create new ShipmentReceipt records for:
  - remaining shipment quantities, and
  - leftover “over-received” quantity (without shipment references).
